completeness.why: Every action takes its category set from isMonthFillTarget/getMonthFillCategories (income-in-tracking rule and hidden rules included, with the hidden SQL removed from the average queries), passing only an explicit scope, and both sign inversions go through spendingToBudgetAmount; copyPreviousMonth keeps its own budget-row query, but that query does no selection and the shared predicate decides it.

interface.why: A single scope parameter ('all' | 'visible' | 'not-hidden') names exactly the three behaviours that exist today, with a comment spelling out the setZero and missing-group inconsistencies, plus a one-purpose sign helper; no speculative options.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated income checks, hidden SQL filters and sign flips are removed into the shared predicate, loader and spendingToBudgetAmount rather than restated.
